finding: buffer_unordered(4) on region stream creates up to 4 concurrent region collection futures, all boxed with Box::pin
impact: Each boxed future allocates heap memory; with many regions this is moderate allocation but bounded
fix: Consider replacing Box::pin with generic future types to eliminate heap allocation for each spawned task

finding: buffer_unordered(10) on service stream creates up to 10 concurrent service collector futures per region
impact: Combined with 4 regions, up to 40 concurrent collector tasks, all serialized through rate limiter
fix: Verify rate limiter handles 40 concurrent operations appropriately; current configuration should be sufficient

finding: tokio::try_join!(regional, global, supplemental) runs three independent futures concurrently
impact: If any future errors, all three are dropped; errors from dropped futures are not reported
fix: Use tokio::select! or join! with error aggregation if all failures need to be reported

finding: tokio::join!(collect, write) waits for both producer and consumer tasks simultaneously
impact: Correct pipeline pattern; channel backpressure (WRITER_QUEUE=4) prevents unbounded growth
fix: None needed; this is the intended producer-consumer pattern

finding: buffer_unordered(PROFILE_CONCURRENCY=4) on job stream creates up to 4 concurrent job collectors
impact: Bounded concurrency is appropriate for profile-based parallelism

finding: Each collect_job creates a dedicated mpsc channel (capacity 1) between AWS collector and event forwarder
impact: Per-job channels provide isolation; when scan completes, sender drops and receiver stream naturally ends
fix: None needed; this is a clean bounded producer-consumer pattern per job

finding: stream::unfold wraps channel receiver into an iterator stream that completes on recv() == None
impact: Correct pattern; stream terminates when sender is dropped (scan completion or cancellation)

finding: Each bucket holds a Mutex<PacingState> for rate state management
impact: Mutex is acquired and released quickly (no async operations while held); contention risk is low
fix: Consider lock-free structures or sharded state if profiling shows contention under high load

finding: acquire order is: local bucket permit -> sequence permit -> global permit
impact: All requests follow same acquisition order, preventing deadlock; however, sequence permit is held while waiting for global, which could cause brief serialization
fix: Consider acquiring global permit before sequence if global is the scarcer resource

finding: tokio::select! with biased ensures cancellation and bucket rejection are prioritized over semaphore acquisition
impact: Cancellation is observed promptly; requests don't spin waiting for permits when the executor is shutting down

finding: Mutex<Option<redis::RedisError>> used to propagate the last error from the send closure across retry attempts
impact: Functional but awkward; Mutex is only accessed serially within a single execute() call, so the lock is unnecessary
fix: Replace with a plain Option and pass by ref mut, or restructure to return the error directly from the closure

finding: Redis connection is taken from projection, passed to executor closure, and returned connection is stored back
impact: Connection is properly reused across batches; closure captures previous connection via FnMut semantics

finding: RequestRecord::drop increments cancelled counter if complete() was not called
impact: Provides safety net for uncompleted operations, but could mask logic errors where complete() is forgotten
fix: Consider adding a debug_assert! in drop to flag programming errors during development

finding: tokio::join! runs organization discovery and supplemental source discovery concurrently
impact: Both futures run to completion regardless of errors in either; errors are handled in post-processing
fix: Consider using tokio::select! if one discovery type should short-circuit the other on error

finding: ApiExecutor uses AtomicU64 for nonce to provide unique request identifiers
impact: Lock-free counter ensures uniqueness without contention
